title: add real-time eval webhook and decision buffer
author: Priya Kapoor
description:
Motivation: Production teams need faster feedback from smoke-eval runs to reduce incident-to-detection time for prompt regressions. Current eval runs produce batch reports that are processed minutes later and can trigger noisy alerts. This PR adds a lightweight real-time eval webhook sink plus a short-lived decision buffer that deduplicates and debounces alerts before they hit the alerting pipeline.

What this changes (high level): Adds a webhook endpoint and client library to emit per-prompt evaluation events in near real time; implements an in-process Redis-backed decision buffer (TTL 60s by default) that collapses repeated failures for the same prompt+metric pair and outputs a single aggregated decision to downstream webhook consumers; wires the buffer into the existing CI eval runner so smoke runs can opt into realtime delivery.

Key design points: 1) Best-effort delivery: the webhook client retries with exponential backoff and falls back to writing to the historical results store if webhook is unreachable. 2) Low-risk defaults: realtime is opt-in per-prompt-set and disabled for long-running full-evals. 3) Short decision window: default TTL keeps the debounce window small to preserve responsiveness while reducing flapping alerts. 4) Observability: added per-event histograms and a small decision buffer gauge to the metrics pipeline.

Acceptance criteria / checklist:
- [x] webhook client + server contract documented in repo docs (docs/realtime-webhook.md)
- [x] decision buffer implementation with pluggable backend (Redis default)
- [x] unit tests for buffer behavior (collapse, expire, flush)
- [x] integration test that simulates noisy failures and asserts single delivery
- [x] CI smoke job updated to exercise realtime path in a short run
- [x] metrics emitted and visible in dev Grafana dashboard

Backward compatibility notes: Feature is opt-in; existing consumers unaffected unless they enable the realtime sink. The public webhook schema is versioned (v1) to allow future extension.

Security notes: Webhooks use a HMAC header; the buffer only stores small serialization keys and decisions (no model inputs).

Testing and rollout plan: Start flag-enabled rollout to internal dev clusters for a week, then enable for a subset of production prompt-sets with monitoring and an emergency kill-switch in the Console.

If merged this will reduce alert noise for repeated regression flickers, and shorten time-to-first-notice for prompt regressions.
commits: a1f4d9c: add webhook client and server skeleton; b3284ae: implement decision buffer with Redis backend and TTL; 9d7b2fa: integrate buffer into smoke-runner; 4c0a1b7: add metrics and tests; ef12b34: docs and changelog
review_comments:
Ethan Morales: Can you clarify the failure modes if Redis is unavailable? Priya Kapoor: Buffer falls back to writing a compressed tombstone to the historical results store and emits a metrics counter; added more detail in code comments and docs.

Liu Zhang: The HMAC secret rotation story? Priya Kapoor: Webhook client reads secrets from KMS-backed env var, rotation via Console toggles; documented.

Marissa Chen: Are we sure TTL=60s is the right default for all workloads? Priya Kapoor: 60s chosen after local replay tests to balance suppression vs responsiveness; made TTL configurable per-prompt-set and left it as a runtime config.

Review outcome: small nits addressed (metric name consistency, added one extra unit test), all reviewers approved.
release_notes: Add opt-in realtime eval webhook and short-lived decision buffer to reduce event flapping and provide faster regression notifications. Configurable TTL and Redis-backed buffer with documented fallback behavior.
notes_for_ops: Deployment requires a Redis instance (can be shared non-critical cluster) or the in-memory fallback for single-node dev. Ensure webhook HMAC secret is provisioned in KMS before enabling. Update Grafana to include new metric eval_realtime.buffer_size_gauge.
